chapters.1: Habakkuk complains to God about the violence and injustice he sees in his own nation going unpunished. God answers that he is already raising up the fierce Babylonians (Chaldeans) to bring judgment, which only troubles Habakkuk further since that nation is even more wicked.
chapters.2: Habakkuk waits for God's response and receives the famous answer that the righteous will live by faith, and that the proud and violent will eventually be brought down. The chapter pronounces a series of "woes" against exploitation, violence, and idolatry, ending with the assurance that the earth will one day be filled with the knowledge of the Lord's glory.
chapters.3: The book closes with Habakkuk's prayer, recalling God's awesome power displayed in Israel's past history, nature trembling at his presence. Despite his fear and the hardship still coming, Habakkuk declares he will rejoice in God and trust him as his strength, even if everything else fails.
